summary: Suspect A and Suspect B acted together: A entered the flat while B waited/assisted remotely by phone; A fired the shot and fled.
explanation_chain: Candidate scenario: Suspect A and Suspect B acted together: A entered the flat while B waited/assisted remotely by phone; A fired the shot and fled.
7 finding(s) support this scenario:

• [ballistics_agent] Single gunshot trajectory reconstructed: firing origin ~[3.1, 2.4, 1.0] near the sofa in the living room, entry angle 14.5° into the west wall (evidence E-03). (confidence 0.82) — Shell casing E-02 and bullet impact E-03 are geometrically consistent with a single shot fired from close range while standing/seated near the sofa, not from the doorway or kitchen entry point. This constrains the shooter's position at the moment of firing to within ~1m of the estimated origin.

• [timeline_agent] Witness-reported gunshot time, victim's estimated time-of-death window, and P-02's near-scene cell activity all fall within the same ~20-30 minute span with no contradicting alibi evidence on file. (confidence 0.75) — Three independently-collected sources (medical, eyewitness, telecom) are temporally consistent with each other. This convergence strengthens confidence in the overall timeline, though it does not by itself assign responsibility — consistency is necessary but not sufficient for a specific scenario to be correct.

• [digital_forensics_agent] Suspect A's device pinged 40m from the scene at 21:47, inside the estimated time-of-death window. (confidence 0.70) — Cell-tower proximity places Suspect A at/near the scene during the window in which the victim is estimated to have died. This is consistent with physical presence but is not, by itself, proof of presence — tower triangulation has meter-to-hundreds-of-meter uncertainty depending on tower density.

• [digital_forensics_agent] Suspect A moved from ~40m to 900m from the scene by 22:10, consistent with departure shortly after the witness-observed person left the stairwell (~21:50). (confidence 0.60) — Movement pattern (arrival near scene -> presence during TOD window -> rapid departure) matches the witness account of someone leaving in a hurry, though it does not independently confirm identity.

• [network_agent] Suspect A and Suspect B are directly connected in the network (relation: known_associate, plus a recorded call during the case window). (confidence 0.58) — A pre-existing known-associate relationship between the two persons of interest, combined with contact during the incident window, increases the structural plausibility of a joint-action scenario (S2) relative to the two being unconnected strangers. This is circumstantial network evidence, not direct proof of coordination in this specific act.

• [digital_forensics_agent] Outgoing call from Suspect A to Suspect B at 21:52, 40m from the scene, duration 65s — roughly 5-7 minutes after the witness-reported gunshot. (confidence 0.55) — A phone contact between the two persons of interest occurring shortly after the estimated time of the shooting, while the caller was still near the scene, is consistent with a coordination/joint-action scenario (S2). It is also consistent with an innocent, unrelated call — call content/transcript would be needed to move beyond circumstantial weight. This finding should not be treated as conclusive on its own.

• [ballistics_agent] Footwear impression E-04 (Partial shoe print, size UK 9-10, tread pattern photographed) is consistent with shoe size range that includes: Suspect A (UK 9.5); Suspect B (UK 10). (confidence 0.45) — Impression size/tread class narrows the pool of plausible individuals but a partial print alone cannot uniquely identify a wearer — this is corroborating, not conclusive, evidence. It should be weighted alongside digital-forensics and timeline findings, not read in isolation.
